title: Private DR: add restore validation gate (health checks + API smoke tests)
author: Diego Santos
description:
Context: During restore drills we had multiple cases where `restore execute` completed successfully but the cluster was not actually usable (API accepting connections but failing auth/migrations, or control-plane pods not ready). This PR adds a validation gate at the end of restore that runs targeted health checks + minimal API smoke tests against the Private API endpoints. If any *critical* checks fail, the restore exits non-zero and prints a clear operator action list.

What this adds: 1) A new validation runner invoked by default at the end of `rw-private-dr restore execute` (can be disabled with `--no-validate`). 2) Health checks for core control-plane dependencies (Postgres connectivity, migration completion signal, control-plane deployments ready). 3) API smoke tests (read-only and tiny write) to prove the API is reachable and behaving correctly post-restore. 4) A machine-readable restore report (`restore-report.json`) written to the same output directory used by other DR artifacts.

Critical vs non-critical checks: - Critical (fail restore): control plane API `/healthz` ready, auth handshake, config/policy read path, DB read/write, control-plane deployments ready, maintenance mode cleared. - Non-critical (warn only): audit export destination reachability, external integration endpoints (SIEM/webhooks), optional metrics endpoints.

Implementation details: - Validation is implemented in `pkg/dr/validate` with a small interface so we can add/remove checks without changing CLI wiring. - API tests use the same endpoint + TLS config as the restore flow, and require an operator-provided token (same as existing restore commands). Requests are intentionally small (`max_tokens=1`) to avoid cost/latency surprises in constrained environments. - All requests have bounded timeouts + retries with exponential backoff. - Output is a checklist-style summary for operators + JSON report for evidence capture.

Operator UX: - On failure we print: which check failed, last error, where to find logs, and next actions (including a hint to re-run `rw-private-dr restore validate --verbose` after fixes). - On success we print the restore artifact IDs and the last-success timestamp.

Security: - No secrets are persisted in the report. - Authorization headers are redacted in logs. - We only hit cluster-local endpoints; no outbound network requirements are introduced.

Testing: - Unit tests for check classification + timeout behavior. - Integration test updates to run the validate step in kind-based restore harness.

Release notes: Restore now fails fast if the cluster is not actually healthy after restore; operators can bypass validation with `--no-validate` (not recommended except for break-glass triage).

Follow-ups (not in this PR): - Emit validation metrics as Prometheus counters/histograms from the job runner (tracked in ENG-4869). - Extend smoke tests for on-prem/air-gapped staging repos once local bundle restore is fully wired (tracked separately).

snippet:
Example output (failure):

$ rw-private-dr restore execute --from s3://rw-backups/cluster-a/2025-10-17T0200Z
...
Restore completed. Running validation gate (11 checks)...
[PASS] control-plane.deployments.ready
[PASS] db.postgres.read
[PASS] db.postgres.write
[FAIL] api.smoke.auth_and_generation (critical)
  error: POST https://redwood-private-api.redwood.svc.cluster.local/v1/chat/completions: 503 Service Unavailable
  hint: check api-gateway logs; confirm maintenance mode is cleared; confirm migrations completed

Validation failed (1 critical, 2 warnings). Restore marked FAILED.
Report: /var/lib/redwood/dr/restore-report.json

Example output (success):

Restore completed. Running validation gate (11 checks)...
[PASS] ...
Validation succeeded.
Report: /var/lib/redwood/dr/restore-report.json
conversation:
Rafael Mendes (SRE) — 2025-10-15: This is the right direction. Two asks: (1) make the API smoke test payload as small as possible (we should not accidentally run a large generation inside a restore job). (2) retries should cap at a fixed wall-clock so we don’t exceed maintenance windows.

Diego Santos — 2025-10-15: Updated `api_smoke.go` to use `max_tokens=1`, `temperature=0`, and a 2s request timeout with a 90s total budget per check. Also added a top-level `--validate-timeout` override for operators.

Ethan Park — 2025-10-16: Can we ensure we don’t run smoke tests while maintenance mode is still enabled? Right now restore flips maintenance mode off late in the sequence, but if that fails we’d get noisy errors.

Diego Santos — 2025-10-16: Added an explicit `maintenance_mode.cleared` check as critical and ordered it before API smoke tests. If the mode is still on, we fail with an actionable message and skip the later API calls.

Allison Grant — 2025-10-16: For evidence capture, JSON report should include timestamps + durations per check. Also please ensure errors are single-line (log ingestion).

Diego Santos — 2025-10-16: Done. Report now includes `started_at`, `finished_at`, and `duration_ms` per check, with `error` normalized to a single line.

Connor O'Brien — 2025-10-17: One nit: default behavior changes (restore can now fail). Please add release note text to README + mention `--no-validate` break-glass.

Diego Santos — 2025-10-17: Added in README under DR commands and in the `restore execute --help` output.

Rafael Mendes — 2025-10-18: Re-ran integration test; looks good. Approved.
